title: Lifting morphisms between canonical formal glueing objects
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings and $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, and suppose the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor with the canonical object components $S\otimes_R M,M_{f_i},c^M_{f_i},\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$ and map components $1\otimes h,h_{f_i}$, with bundled equalities and heterogeneous equalities of the actual structural and component maps as in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For any $R$-modules $M,N$ and any morphism $z:\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ there exists an $R$-linear map $h:M\to N$ with $\mathrm{Can}(h)=z$. This asserts surjectivity only, not uniqueness or essential surjectivity.

proof.text: Transport the given morphism z to an S-linear prime map p and R-linear chart maps c_i, using the object equalities. canonical_piece_eq identifies the restricted chart module structure with the standard localized R-module by algebraMap_smul; transport_prime and transport_chart produce HEqs of components.

For each m, canonical_tuple_compatible puts the component tuple into the kernel of beta. Apply formalGlueingComplexExact to N: exactness produces n with alpha(n) equal to the tuple, and injectivity makes n unique. Projecting this equality gives the prime and chart value equations.

Define value(m) by the unique preimage from the preceding step. Additivity of tensoring by 1, localization and p,c shows that value(x)+value(y) has the required component values for x+y, hence uniqueness gives additivity. Similarly tensor scalar balancing and S-linearity of p give the prime scalar equation, and R-linearity of c gives the chart scalar equations; uniqueness gives value(rm)=r value(m). Bundle these into an R-linear map h. The chosen object is determined uniquely, not chosen from arbitrary existence.

Tensor induction, the equation for 1 tensor m and S-linearity show extendMap(phi,h)=p. IsLocalizedModule.ext and the equations at m/1 show localMap(fi,h)=c_i. Compose these equalities with hmap and the transported-component HEqs to obtain equality of the prime and all chart components of Can.map(h) and z. components_ext gives equality of the morphisms, hence surjectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem canonical_map_surjective {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hmap : (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (Can.map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom)))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) :
    Function.Surjective (Can.map : (M ⟶ N) → (Can.obj M ⟶ Can.obj N))
